images.title: Tilted rod, then parallel rod
images.purpose: Compare a tilted rod with a shorter projection and the same rod held parallel, whose projection is its full length.
images.composition: Two side views side by side on white, no panel borders: tilted on the left, parallel on the right.
images.exact_structure: Each side has one horizontal dark table line near the bottom. Left: a teal #0072B2 rod 13 cm long slanting up to the right, one end 5 cm higher than the other; dashed grey #6B7280 perpendiculars drop from both ends to the table; the segment between their feet is thick reddish purple #CC79A7 labelled '12 cm'; the rod is labelled '13 cm' and the rise is shown by a short dashed vertical with the label '5 cm'. Right: the same teal rod held flat, parallel to the table, with dashed grey perpendiculars from both ends; the purple projection below it is exactly as long as the rod and is labelled '13 cm'. Under the left side 'tilted', under the right side 'parallel'.

images.takeaway: A tilted rod has a shorter projection; only a parallel rod projects to its full length.
images.description: Compare a tilted rod with a shorter projection and the same rod held parallel, whose projection is its full length.
images.context: One clean concept image for T10.C4.

image_decisions.why: The practice predicts projection lengths; the tilted and parallel cases together show the rule.
